notes:
POC objective: validate Redwood Dedicated can meet Lodestar's production throughput & p95 latency SLOs for customer-facing agent and internal rerank pipelines.

Recent timeline (bullets from AE/SE activity):
- 2025-01-12: Intro call (AE Elena) — high level requirements, shared initial topology diagram.
- 2025-01-20: Technical deep-dive (SE Diego) — target workloads, sample prompts, compliance checklist reviewed (Fireflies: FF_2025-01-20_8241).
- 2025-01-28: Pricing + legal prelim discussion — finance asked for ARR band and reserved-GPU options.
- 2025-02-03: Network & infra sync — network team provided constraints for on-prem connector, egress rules noted.
- 2025-02-05: POC kickoff prep — test harness finalized, representative prompt set uploaded to Drive.

POC / performance plan (explicit acceptance criteria):
- Workloads: customer support chat (multi-turn, avg 6 turns), embeddings for semantic search, reranking for top-N results.
- Representative prompt pack: 50 templates (short queries 32–64 tokens, medium 256 tokens, long 800+ tokens for summarization).
- Throughput targets: sustained 60 qps for chat-short workload; 20 qps for long-context summarization; reranking spikes to 150 qps for batched pairwise scoring.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 400ms for short chat (<=64 tokens), p95 <= 1.5s for medium (<=256 tokens), p95 <= 3.5s for long summarization workloads. Tail-latency budget must be tracked separately (p99 thresholds).
- Capacity planning ask: baseline reserved pool 8x A10-equivalent GPUs with headroom for 2x burst nodes OR equivalent vCPU-backed routing for low-cost fallbacks. SE to produce GPU-hours estimate + cost delta for INT8 vs FP16.
- Load tests: stepped ramp to 2x target qps (120 qps) for 10 minutes bursts to validate autoscaling/burst policies.
- Soak tests: 72-hour steady-state at target qps (60 qps) capturing GPU utilization, token/sec, KV cache hit rates, memory pressure, and request/response sizes.
- Chaos checks: forced worker restarts during soak to validate fallbacks and session persistence (KV cache warmup) and to measure cold-start frequency.
- Quantization experiments: trial INT8 and FP16 profiles on a 1-GPU pilot; validate quality delta on 200 eval prompts, target <2% regression on fidelity metrics.
- Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, per-request cost, batching efficiency (avg batch size), KV cache hit ratio, memory/GPU error rates.

SLA negotiation points raised by Lodestar:
- Explicit p95 latency SLOs by route + credits for sustained breach.
- Clear fallback policy (model variants / downgraded quantization) before customer-visible degradation.
- Reserved capacity commitment window (monthly vs annual) and burst capacity pricing.
- Data residency clause for embeddings storage and audit log retention.

Open questions / blockers captured in CRM:
- Security team requested SOC2 Type II evidence for Redwood-hosted telemetry within POC window (have partial docs in Drive).
- Legal wants explicit indemnity language around model outputs (pending).
- Lodestar infra wants a validated private connector topology for on-prem fallback (network team to provide firewall rules).

Next steps agreed with customer (short bullets):
- SE to run initial 1-GPU bench with 10k synthetic prompts (Due: 2025-02-07).
- Redwood to provision Dedicated pilot cluster and share temporary credentials for POC (ETA: 2025-02-10).
- Lodestar security to provide list of required audit artifacts; exp to close by 2025-02-12.
- AE to deliver reserved-GPU sizing + pricing options after soak (Due: 2025-02-14).

Customer quotes / color: "If we can hit p95 targets under steady load with predictable unit costs, we can push Dedicated into procurement this quarter." — Head of ML Ops.

CRM shorthand / quick flags:

- Cost-sensitive: wants INT8 proof vs quality.
- Timeline: Procurement window Q1, forecasted close 2025-03.

Linked artifacts (stubs): pricing deck, POC prompt pack, security checklist (Drive).
